title: Serious injuries don't just "happen"
summary: NH argues that serious 'freak' injuries don't strike natural lifters out of nowhere: they come from attempting weights far beyond anything you've handled, or from overuse injuries signalled well in advance by chronic pain. He advises staying in manageable rep ranges and leaving a rep in the tank, links tendon ruptures mainly to PED use, and admits his own injuries came from ignoring warning signs.

claims.claim: Natural lifters who train smart won't suffer a sudden career-ending injury; 'freak' injuries come from doing something freakishly stupid like loading far too much weight.
Don't attempt weights you've never come close to: if you squat 275 lb for 4, don't put 315 on the bar for a single.
Bodybuilders should stay in rep ranges they can control and always leave one rep in the tank; powerlifters chase 1RMs but should still pick attainable attempts based on how weights feel.
If NH can deadlift 450 lb for 3, he does only 2.
Tendons, muscles and bones don't just give way mid-curl; serious injuries are preceded by overuse injuries signalled by chronic pain.
Severe chronic tendinitis is a deep pain inside the tendon felt all day, not a prickly feeling; it develops progressively and at its worst can lead to rupture.
Most people who rupture a pec or biceps tendon are not natural: PEDs sharply raise rupture risk by weakening tendons and overgrowing muscle beyond what the skeletal system can support.
Watching injury videos makes lifters fear sudden tears, but for naturals there will be warning signals; listen to your body and you won't get hurt.

Every injury NH had built up over time; he ignored the signals and powered through, and snapped his patellar tendon, broke ribs and hurt his shoulder, all of which listening to pain could have prevented.
